name: Knight Sword Swap AI Video: The Big Knight Takes the Heavy Sword
blurb: The knight sword swap AI video remakes a viral knight reel with your own cast.

prompts.label: 1. The video prompt is filled in. Settings: Seedance 2.5, 10 s, 720p, 9:16, sound on. The video prompt
prompts.text:
A slow, tender, cinematic scene from a real fantasy film, shot on 35mm with natural film grain and muted grey-green colors, on a wide, misty moor of long, wet, green grass with thick fog hiding the horizon, soft grey light and a strong wind from the left. One continuous shot with no cuts: the camera stays low with a slight handheld sway, at a medium shot, so both faces stay large and clear until the end.

The little knight is the one in [Image 1], in every frame: copy the exact face from [Image 1] (the face shape, eye color and eye shape, eyebrows, nose, mouth, cheeks, skin tone, hair color, hair length and hairstyle) and keep their real age and small size. Keep each child's gender from [Image 1]: a boy stays a boy and a girl stays a girl, with the same hair length as in [Image 1], also when the wind blows the hair; no long hair, bow or hair clip unless [Image 1] shows them. If [Image 1] shows a baby, keep the same baby at the same age, with the same face, eyes, nose, mouth, cheeks, skin tone and hair, standing upright as a tiny knight: never an older child. If [Image 1] shows an animal, the little knight is that animal standing upright in small fitted armor, with its own face, fur and markings, never a person. Leave out temporary marks on the skin, like scratches, bruises, stickers or food.
The big knight is the adult in [Image 2], in every frame: copy the exact face from [Image 2] (the face shape, eye color and eye shape, eyebrows, nose, mouth, skin tone, age, hair color, hair length and hairstyle, and any beard, moustache, glasses or freckles).
The little knight is always the child or the pet, and the big knight is always the adult: if [Image 1] shows an adult and [Image 2] shows a child, the child from [Image 2] is the little knight and the adult from [Image 1] is the big knight. Never put an adult's face on the little knight's small body.
Never blend the two faces. Each face stays the same from the first frame to the last, so the family recognizes them at once.

The little knight wears small fitted silver plate armor and a short cream cape, with no helmet, no bow and no hair clip. The big knight wears polished silver plate armor with no helmet and a long dark red cape, and holds {object}. The big knight has no sword.

At the start the little knight stands in front and grips the hilt of a heavy steel longsword with both hands at chest height, point to the sky, just beside the face; the blade rises far above the head. The little knight keeps the eyes wide open and frowns bravely against the wind with lips pressed together, struggling to hold the heavy, tall sword upright while the wind blows the hair and the cape. The little knight never cries and never screams. The big knight, a few steps behind and to the right, walks slowly forward, kneels on one knee beside the little knight, gently takes the heavy sword from the little hands and gives the little knight {object}. The little knight hugs it tight with a small, relieved smile. The big knight stands up, plants the sword point-down in the grass with one hand and rests the other hand on the little knight's shoulder, standing guard while the long red cape streams in the wind. Both look out into the mist, faces turned three-quarters to the camera.

Audio: howling wind, the cape flapping, soft clinks of armor, and an original slow, emotional orchestral score with sweeping strings, epic and tender. No dialogue, no lyrics. Exactly two figures and one sword, nobody in the background, no extra limbs, no morphing, no text, no logos.

Use the two uploaded images as the base. The one in the first image is the little knight. The one in the second image is the big knight. Keep each face, facial features, skin tone and hair (or fur) exactly the same as in their own photo, and keep the little one's age and size. Do not blend the two. If the first image shows an animal, the little knight is that animal standing upright in small fitted armor. If the first image shows a baby, keep the same baby at the same age, with the same face, eyes, nose, mouth, cheeks, skin tone and hair, standing upright as a tiny knight. Leave out temporary marks on the skin, like scratches, bruises, stickers or food, but keep birthmarks, moles and freckles. A still from a real film on a wide, misty moor of long, wet, green grass, with thick fog hiding the horizon, soft grey light and a strong wind from the left. In the front, the little knight stands in small fitted silver plate armor and a short ivory cape that whips in the wind, holding the hilt of a heavy steel longsword with both hands at chest height, point to the sky, just beside the face; the blade rises far above the head. The little knight faces the camera with big, wide-open eyes and a calm, brave little face: small, but brave, not crying. The eyes are open and clearly visible. No bow, no hair clip. A few steps behind and to the right, the big knight stands tall in shining golden plate armor over fine chainmail, with no helmet, and a long, sheer ivory cape with gold embroidery streaming in the wind. The big knight holds {object} and smiles a soft, loving smile, the face turned three-quarters toward the camera. The big knight has no sword. Low camera at the little knight's eye level. Both full body, both faces clear and sharp. Photorealistic, natural film grain, muted grey-green colors, not CGI. Vertical 9:16. Exactly two figures, nobody in the background, no text, no logos.
